content.text:
Resubmitted with the unmet element repaired in operative language.

**Repairs made this round:**

1. **"Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law."** — no longer relies on the two-step materiality chain of retained 14.1(c) plus the Section 13.4(b) covenant. Section 14.1 now carries an express limb **"(f) RevMed's breach of Applicable Law;"**, mirroring the narrowed Section 14.2(b) and removing the asymmetry the verifier identified. Coverage for this element is now `addressed_by_operation` (ops 1 and 2), not `already_met`.
2. **Cross-reference conformed** — the Section 14.1 exception lead-in now reads "except in each case ((a) through (f))", covering all six limbs, so nothing dangles.
3. **IP limb restated as a claim-based trigger** — "(d) any Third Party Claim alleging that the RevMed Licensed Technology, or Sanofi's exercise of the licenses granted to it under this Agreement, infringes or misappropriates the intellectual property rights of a Third Party", using the Section 1.99 defined term. This is the correct analogue to "Services or Deliverables" in a research/licence agreement with no services construct, and it answers the Section 13.5 non-infringement disclaimer.

**Unchanged and deliberate:** Section 14.2 remains narrowed to Sanofi-provided content and Sanofi's breach of Applicable Law (with (c)/(d) marked "[Intentionally omitted.]" so the "(a) through (d)" flush carve-out still reads); no procure/modify/replace, refund or 3× super-cap is proposed, because taking the fallback would cap an indemnity that Section 14.5 currently leaves uncapped and "annual fees" has no analogue in this upfront/milestone/royalty deal; and the favourable notice, control-of-defence and cost-reimbursed cooperation machinery in Section 14.3 is untouched.
